$comment: R1728 — the analysis tool's navigation, written down once, in neutral
vocabulary, as the behaviour reference draws it.
WHY THIS IS A FILE AND NOT A RUST CONSTANT. The application's rail is a
Rust table (`spec::RAIL`) because a seat needs facts a specification does
not fix: its icon, its page, the wording of its refusal. If the
specification lived beside it, written by the same hand in the same edit,
a conformance test would be asking the thing under test for the answer.
It is a separate artifact, reviewed as a claim about the reference rather
than as code.
EXTRACTION. The reference is not in this repository and must not be. The
procedure is thirty seconds and is recorded in the session memory note on
the behaviour reference: the three delivered screens each draw the same
rail, so pulling the seat list off any one of them and checking the other
two agree is the whole of it. Measured 2026-08-19: eight seats, identical
order on all three screens, and the only difference between the screens is
which seat is marked current.
VOCABULARY. The reference's product, protocol and resource words are
replaced by the words the tool class uses generally. Structure and
behaviour are what is being reproduced; the wording is not.
THE TWO HALVES. `canon` is what the reference does. `owed` is where this
build does not do it yet, each entry carrying why. The gate asserts the
difference between the built rail and `canon` is EXACTLY `owed` — so a new
divergence fails, and so does an owed one that has been paid off without
this file being told. The second direction is the one that keeps the
number honest.

$owed_comment: `sentence` is the divergence VERBATIM, as the framework renders it. That
is deliberate and it is the ratchet: any change to the built rail, and any
change to how a divergence is worded, makes the gate fail until somebody
reads this file and decides what the new sentence should be. A looser
match — the key alone, or a substring — would let a seat drift from
`elsewhere` to `unbuilt`, or from renamed to absent, without a word.
